name: Two-Stage Choice and Rated Referent Likelihood
summary: Listeners first choose the referent they think the speaker means, then rate the likelihood of a probed referent on a 7-point scale.

charter.question: Does probing both a listener's top referent choice and their graded endorsement of a specific competitor referent distinguish recursive pragmatic reasoning from competitor-confusion and oddity heuristics?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this study you will look at groups of friendly robots and figure out which robot a speaker is talking about.
instructions.task: On each screen you will see several robots. First, click the robot you think the speaker means when they say a word (or before they speak). Second, rate how likely a highlighted robot is from 1 (not at all likely) to 7 (extremely likely).

comprehension_checks.question: What are the two steps on each screen?
options: First click the robot you think the speaker means, then rate how likely the highlighted robot is from 1 to 7.
Click every robot on the screen.
Type a word for each robot.

comprehension_checks.question: Can the speaker see the same group of robots that you see?
options: Yes, the speaker sees the exact same robots.
No, the speaker only sees one robot.
No, the speaker cannot see the screen.
